# Third-party skills: Emil Kowalski design engineering

Copied unchanged from [emilkowalski/skills](https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills) at commit `c8a79627b59d72d764d6ab6f2c87c09a48169833` (2026-11-04), MIT License (see `LICENSE`).

These encode a high craft bar for UI polish and motion. Examples are often React/CSS; apply the principles to BattleQuest's plain TypeScript, HTML overlay and Pixi board.

| Skill                          | Use in BattleQuest                                                             |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `emil-design-eng`              | The overall polish philosophy: the invisible details that make UI feel premium |
| `animate`                      | Building one animation: should it animate, easing, duration, origin            |
| `choreograph`                  | Several things moving together: radial petals, card fans, unlock sequences     |
| `review-animations`            | Strict review of motion work before it ships                                   |
| `animation-performance`        | Staying inside the frame budget on tablets                                     |
| `apple-design`                 | Fluid, gesture-driven, interruptible motion                                    |
| `mobile-native`                | Making the web build feel like a native app on phones and tablets              |
| `animation-vocabulary`         | Turning a vague request ("the bouncy thing") into the exact technique          |
| `find-animation-opportunities` | Audit for places that should (or shouldn't) animate                            |

Not copied: `animate-expo`, `write-swift`, `ask-sonner`, `pick-ui-library`, `prototype`, `break-ui`, `remove-animations`, `improve-animations` (React Native, Swift, React-only libraries, or overlapping audits).

When these disagree with the project's `motion` skill or `docs/UX_PRESENTATION.md`, the project wins.
